user_question: Calculate total population and land area by census tract across Centre County.

workflow_plan.goal: Calculate total population and land area by census tract across Centre County.

workflow_steps.title: Aggregate population by census tract
workflow_steps.purpose: Compute total population for each census tract from the supplied ACS attribute table.
workflow_steps.instructions: Group the supplied table by the observed tract identifier field and sum the observed total population field. Preserve the tract identifier and emit one summarized row per tract. Runtime QC must verify the actual schema fields before execution.

workflow_steps.title: Retrieve tract-level land-area table
workflow_steps.purpose: Obtain a candidate attribute table containing land area by Centre County census tract for joining to the supplied tract geometries.
workflow_steps.instructions: Retrieve the highest-ranked available CSV table with land-area values keyed by census tract and coverage of Centre County. Treat the result as a candidate only; runtime QC must inspect its schema, tract-key compatibility, spatial coverage, and land-area field before downstream use. Do not infer or rename fields.

workflow_steps.title: Join population totals to census tracts
workflow_steps.purpose: Attach the aggregated population totals to the supplied census tract geometries.
workflow_steps.instructions: Join the supplied tract vector with the population summary table using the compatible observed tract identifier fields. Leave vector_key and table_key unset until runtime schema QC grounds the actual fields.

workflow_steps.title: Join land area to population-enriched tracts
workflow_steps.purpose: Produce the final census-tract vector containing both total population and land-area attributes.
workflow_steps.instructions: Join the population-enriched tract vector with the retrieved land-area attribute table using the compatible observed tract identifier fields. Leave vector_key and table_key unset until runtime schema QC grounds the actual fields. Preserve the tract geometries and both analytical attributes.
